title: Cohomology of the sequential derived limit
statement:
Let $\mathcal R$ be a sheaf of rings on $X_{\mathrm{proét}}$, let
$\cdots\to K_2\xrightarrow{t_1}K_1\xrightarrow{t_0}K_0$ be a tower of complexes of
$\mathcal R$-modules, $T\colon\prod_nK_n\to\prod_nK_n$, $T((k_n)_n)=(t_n(k_{n+1}))_n$, and
$R\varprojlim_nK_n:=\operatorname{Cone}(1-T)[-1]$.

1. For every $q$ there is a natural short exact sequence of sheaves

   $$
   0\to\coker\Bigl(\prod_nH^{q-1}(K_n)\xrightarrow{1-T}\prod_nH^{q-1}(K_n)\Bigr)
   \to H^q\bigl(R\varprojlim_nK_n\bigr)\to\varprojlim_nH^q(K_n)\to0 .
   $$

2. For a tower of modules $(M_n)$ (complexes in degree $0$), $R^p\varprojlim_nM_n:=
   H^p(R\varprojlim_nM_n)$ is $\varprojlim_nM_n$ for $p=0$,
   $\coker(1-T)$ for $p=1$, and $0$ for $p\notin\{0,1\}$.
3. Consequently the sequence in 1 is the Milnor sequence
   $0\to R^1\varprojlim_nH^{q-1}(K_n)\to H^q(R\varprojlim_nK_n)\to\varprojlim_nH^q(K_n)\to0$.

proof.text: Apply exact countable products for pro-etale module sheaves, then the generic natural Roos cohomology sequence. Its explicit maps arise from the cone long exact sequence, its kernel/cokernel factorization, the projection-induced product/homology comparison, and the kernel-to-limit comparison.

For a tower of modules in degree zero, the homology tower vanishes in every degree other than zero, and its degree-zero tower is naturally isomorphic to the original tower. At q=0 the left endpoint of the generic short exact sequence vanishes, so its projection is an isomorphism onto the limit. At q=1 its right endpoint vanishes, so its inclusion is an isomorphism from the cokernel. Transport these by the natural degree-zero homology tower isomorphism. In every other degree both endpoints vanish, hence so does the middle. Naturality of the resulting two isomorphisms follows by composing the sequence squares with this natural tower isomorphism and using inverse isomorphism cancellation.

For each q retain the same inclusion and projection from the generic sequence. Precompose its inclusion with the degree-one isomorphism for the tower H^(q-1)(K). Transport short exactness through this isomorphism of short complexes. This proves the final clause with the same maps as the first clause.

Steps 1, 2, 3 and 6 are correct. I recomputed the cone: D^r=A^r+B^{r-1} with differential (d_A a, -d_B b - phi a), and d^2=0. For a degree-0 tower, D has P in degrees 0,1 with differential -(1-T), so H^0=lim, H^1=coker, and every other degree is 0. The product comparison is rederived from det-pe-products-exact through cycles and boundaries. The only statement nodes used are from the cited unit sk-prop-pe-products, plus the Mathlib leaf lem-sf-derived-homology-long-exact; no tool_uses are needed. No new nodes, no statement change, no SGA. Edge cases checked: zero tower; zero transitions; constant tower; the tower p^nZ in Z, which gives coker(1-T)=Z_p/Z, nonzero. No Mittag-Leffler or epimorphism hypothesis is used. Two minor C4/E5 repairs. (1) Step 4 took products of module sheaves to be computed sectionwise, which no cited node states; it now derives ker(1-T)=lim from the universal properties of kernel and product (uses += def-weil-category-product). (2) Step 5's naturality took the connecting map gamma to be H^q of the negative projection, but the long-exact-sequence node's statement only says connecting maps exist. I added that its Mathlib match DerivedCategory.HomologySequence.δ is shiftMap of T.mor₃ (checked in HomologySequence.lean lines 152-155), with uses += lem-sf-derived-homology-long-exact.
